en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers.
Laguna de Bay in the CALABARZON region is the largest lake in the Philippines and the third largest in Southeast Asia.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area and is often called the country's last ecological frontier.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its high marine biodiversity.
Baguio City, located in the Cordillera Administrative Region, has a subtropical climate making it significantly cooler than most other Philippine cities.
The Philippines is the world's top producer of abaca, a native banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make everyday items like ropes and textiles.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a unique volcano situated on an island within Taal Lake, which fills a massive volcanic caldera.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes that are larger than its brain.
